# Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor

Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `<id>` holding no `/` is this route,

When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage.

- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id, room, title, date, start, end}, ... ]}`. On load, validate strictly (object, integer nextId >= 1, bookings array of well-formed bookings with id < nextId); anything else → `cannot read data file <name>`.

content.text:
I graded `server.mjs`, `package.json` and `test/server.smoke.test.mjs` against `.team/notes/spec.md` (Server, API, Booking rules) and `.team/notes/decisions.md`. `npm test` passes 60 of 60. The project has no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or rules files, so only your standards applied. It passes your bar (9 overall, nothing under 7), and I found no spec bugs. The open items are about style and test gaps.

**Spec checks that hold (`/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs`):**
- **Startup order (338–361):** `PORT` is checked first, then the data file is read, then the server listens. Every failure writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1. The port-in-use case is handled with `exitCode` and a natural exit, so there is no stack trace.
- **Data file name and errors:** `DATA_FILE` is echoed exactly as given, and only `ENOENT` means "no bookings yet". A directory, a bad path argument, invalid JSON or the wrong layout all give `cannot read data file <name>`.
- **Body reading (180–191, 303):** the whole body is read and discarded before any routing, so 413 and 415 replies always reach the client. Rule 2 counts the body bytes actually received.
- **Routing (283–312):** paths are compared byte for byte on the raw `req.url` up to the first `?`. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404, any other `/api/bookings/<id>` reaches DELETE, and HEAD/OPTIONS give 405. Method lookup uses `Object.hasOwn`, so a method named `constructor` cannot slip through.
- **Booking rules:** they run in order 1 to 10 with the exact messages. Only the title is trimmed. Leap years follow year % 4 inside 2000–2099. The 409 picks the clash that starts earliest, not the first one found (101).
- **Saving (161–172, 235–239):** the temp file sits next to the data file and is then renamed over it, and a failed temp file is cleaned up. Memory, including the next id, only changes after a successful save.
- **Concurrency:** the overlap check and the save run inside one promise queue (229–233), and the queue's error catch does not hide errors from callers.
- **500 handling (314–326):** unexpected errors are logged to stderr only (nothing leaks to the client), the reply is 500 `internal error`, and the server keeps running.
- **Static files and stdout:** static files are served from a fixed map resolved from `import.meta.url`, so there is no path traversal. The listening line is the only stdout write.

**Smoke test:** it is strong for its size. Several tests would catch a plausible wrong implementation: the earliest-clash test inserts bookings out of order, `'  hi  '` catches trimStart/trimEnd, the exactly-10000-byte body catches `<` vs `<=`, and there are tests for rollback of the next id and for leftover `.tmp` files. The gaps are listed in the fixes below. I did not measure coverage: the server runs as a child process, so Node's built-in coverage would not see it.

**One stale note:** `decisions.md` still says the test script is `node --test test/`. You said the `"test/**/*.test.mjs"` glob is deliberate and `package.json` is correct, so I did not grade this. Updating the decisions file would avoid confusion later.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear layers (validation, data file, HTTP plumbing, app, startup) and new frozen state objects instead of mutation; createApp holds all request handling in one closure
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent (MSG table, findOverlap, commit, serialize); one cryptic local `q`
duplication: 9 — shared validateFields covers both POST and data-file loading; the stderr + exitCode lines in main appear twice
size: 8 — file is 363 lines and inner functions are small, but createApp (224–327) is about 104 lines, over the 50-line limit
errors: 9 — startup errors are one line with exit 1 and listen errors use err.code; save failures roll back; 500s are logged without leaking and the server stays up
tests: 8 — 21 black-box smoke tests that catch plausible wrong implementations (weighted lightly); no tests for DELETE rollback or strict data-file validation
security: 10 — no secrets, fixed static map with no traversal, body size capped, nothing internal in replies
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:224 split createApp below 50 lines: move listBookings/createBooking/deleteBooking/route to module level and pass in a small store object ({ getState, serialize, commit }) built by a `createStore(dataPath, initialState)` helper
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:305 rename `q` to `queryStart`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:340 merge the two `process.stderr.write(...); process.exitCode = 1; return;` blocks (340–343, 348–351) into one `failStartup(message)` helper
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:264 optional edge case: if `state.nextId + 1` ever passed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, the saved file would fail its own load check on the next start; reject with a 500 before saving
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.smoke.test.mjs:123 add data-file cases the strict loader must reject: a booking with id >= nextId, duplicate ids, an untrimmed title, overlapping stored bookings, extra or missing booking keys
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.smoke.test.mjs:352 add a DELETE-on-save-failure case (create a booking, make the folder unwritable or remove it, DELETE gives 500, and the booking is still listed)
